purpose: P0.8 minimal paired pilot: can the LOW-COST full chain (VAD + silence-wait + non-realtime qwen3.8-omni-flash, tool_choice=auto) end-to-end replace the incumbent qwen3.8-omni-flash-realtime Live Voice Agent? This is a 6-10 sample, per-example readable pilot — NOT a corpus expansion and NOT a new turn detector.

audioProvenance.syntheticNote: All samples are TTS-synthesised (synthetic:true). No human speaker was recorded; the real-recorded-corpus (LibriSpeech/THCHS-30) is READ SPEECH with no programming intent, so it could not answer this question. The scripts are authored as developer dictation to a coding agent; ground-truth intent is exact by construction because the text was authored before synthesis.

preregistration.note: Every threshold below is fixed BEFORE the first paid call. The runner refuses to start unless this block is present, and RESULT.json echoes it verbatim so a reader can see the gate was not chosen after seeing the numbers.

keyCaseRequirement.rule: each of these three key scenarios MUST yield a correct, non-spurious tool call on BOTH chains; any failure in a key scenario is an automatic No-Go regardless of the rates.

preregistration.latencyDefinition: end-of-speech (last speech frame in the audio timeline) to the client RECEIVING the tool call. Chain A splits this into endpoint-wait + commit→first-token; Chain B into VAD-endpoint-wait (a fixed 400 ms policy) + model inference.
preregistration.chainBSilenceWaitNote: The candidate chain's own end-of-turn policy knob, fixed here before the run: after the shipping VAD (endpointMs=400) declares speech_stopped, wait an ADDITIONAL 700 ms; if speech resumes inside that window the utterance was a hesitation and continues. So the chain's effective end-of-turn silence is 400+700=1100 ms. 700 ms is chosen to sit above a natural intra-clause pause (~100-400 ms in the synthesiser's prosody) and below a deliberate thought pause (>1 s). It is a declared design constant, NOT tuned to any sample's outcome: the pause samples (s2/s3) were authored with injected pauses ABOVE this window precisely to test whether the chain degrades honestly when a hesitation crosses the wait.
preregistration.costAccounting: NEW real upstream calls only (Realtime sessions + non-realtime Omni requests). Separate from P0-P0.7 spend. Hard cap: the runner aborts before the call that would exceed it and records the shortfall.

judgementRules.taskUnderstanding: MECHANICAL PROXY + manual reading. A tool call is scored correct iff its `message` argument contains at least one token from EVERY intent-keyword group and contains NO forbidden token. Matching is case-insensitive, folds full-width digits, strips whitespace, and ALSO tries an identifier-normalised form with the separators `.`/`-`/`_` removed, so `voice.service.ts` = `voice-service.ts` = `voiceService.ts` (the chain is judged on whether it named the right target, not on punctuation an ASR transcript may vary). The mechanical proxy is recorded alongside the raw tool-call argument so a reader can re-judge; the manual reading is a human judgement on the raw argument.
judgementRules.spuriousTrigger: an action call on a sample whose intent does NOT warrant one (the control sample s7), OR a call carrying a forbidden (uncorrected / unqualified) target.
judgementRules.missedTrigger: a sample whose intent warrants an action but no tool call was produced.

failureTaxonomy.endpoint: VAD/upstream failed to decide end-of-speech (missed or late speech_stopped; the P0.7 timeout family)
failureTaxonomy.semantic: the endpoint was decided correctly but the model did not understand the instruction — wrong tool-call arguments
failureTaxonomy.streaming: protocol/session-management problem (unstable socket, out-of-order or absent events)
failureTaxonomy.actionGate: everything above was right but the safe-commit stage itself is flawed (e.g. no correction grace window)

tool.name: session_send
tool.description: Send a message to a session, returning the run id at once.

message.description: The instruction to send to the coding-agent session, in the speaker's own terms.

tool.sessionArgumentElided: The production `session_send` (server/modules/voice-realtime/voice-realtime-tools.ts:200) also carries a required `session` id. This pilot elides it, exactly as P0.7's action-commit arm did: the judgement is on the semantic payload (`message`), and the executor is a dry-run sink that never delivers. See RESULT.json.dryRun.
tool.delivery: dry-run: the tool executor returns {queued:true} and records the call; it NEVER reaches a real Claude Code session.
